_: Golden for the au.ausgrid-ea116 preset — D2 §9 1 and 4, D9 §3. Australia's demand window runs every day, not only on weekdays, and only in two seasons.

sources.grammar: HLD §8's AU row: `(30, peak_window, all, max, month, Linear)` — a 30-minute interval, only the peak window eligible, the single highest of the month.
sources.window: ausgrid.com.au/your-energy-use/smarter-energy-use/understanding-network-tariffs/demand-pricing, read 2026-09-19: the peak window is between "3pm and 9pm", "every day", in the "June - August and November - March periods", and the charge is "calculated on the one day of the month during the peak window when the highest 30-minute period of consumption occurs".
sources.price: 44.4147 c/kVA/day peak demand for EA116 in 2026-27 (Ausgrid's 2026-27 indicative network prices, as reported 2026-09-19). Quoted per DAY, which the grammar has no unit for, so it is carried as a year: 0.444147 x 365 = 162.1137 AUD/kVA/year, and `price_period_unit: year` makes the month pay a twelfth, 13.509475. See the preset's `assumed` — a 31-day month really pays more than a 28-day one and this averages that away.
sources.month: Constructed, not measured: July 2026, which is inside the June-August season, and in AEST so no DST seam.
sources.metric_kw: A 30-minute window's kW is twice its kWh: 3.2 -> 6.40, 3.6 -> 7.20, 2.5 -> 5.00. The single highest eligible one is 7.20 kW, and it falls on a Sunday — the window runs every day, so the weekend counts.
sources.not_metric_kw: 10.00 kW, the 5.0 kWh half-hour at 22:00 on 2026-07-08, which is after the window closes at 21:00.

eligibility.why: every day, so a Sunday counts — unlike the US presets
December is in the November-March season
September is a shoulder month in neither season

eligible_windows.why: 15:00-21:00 in half hours is twelve windows
